quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #14
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: You are coming to an intersection with a flashing red light. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and let other drivers go first.
Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.
Stop completely, look both ways, and go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, look both ways, and go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same thing as a stop sign. You must stop completely, let other traffic and pedestrians go first, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: Can you cross a double solid yellow centerline to pass another vehicle?

options.text: Yes.
No.
Only if there is no oncoming traffic.
Only if the vehicle ahead is driving under the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: No.
questions.explanation: Two solid yellow lines mean neither lane can cross them to pass. You can only cross double yellow lines when turning into a driveway or business entrance. You cannot pass over a solid yellow line.

questions.question: When there is a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line, passing is allowed:

options.text: From the side with the solid yellow line.
From neither direction.
From the side with the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: From the side with the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line allows passing from that side. A solid yellow line does not allow passing. So you can only pass from the side next to the broken line.

questions.question: Driving speed does not affect how far your vehicle travels after you brake.

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.correctAnswerText: FALSE
questions.explanation: Speed matters a lot. The faster you drive, the longer it takes your vehicle to stop. Stay far behind the vehicle in front of you when driving fast.

questions.question: What is defensive driving?

options.text: Spotting dangerous situations and taking action to avoid accidents.
Passing bad drivers to get ahead in traffic.
Following the car in front of you closely.
Quickly changing lanes and weaving through traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spotting dangerous situations and taking action to avoid accidents.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means you spot unsafe situations and act before an accident happens. It helps you avoid problems with reckless, careless, or drunk drivers and pedestrians.

questions.question: What will help someone stop feeling the effects of alcohol?

options.text: Tomato juice and lime
Hot coffee
Fresh air
Only time

questions.correctAnswerText: Only time
questions.explanation: Only time will reduce the effects of alcohol on your body.

questions.question: Large vehicles have blind spots that can extend up to 200 feet behind them.

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.correctAnswerText: TRUE
questions.explanation: Large vehicles have blind spots up to 200 feet behind them. Do not tailgate large vehicles because the driver cannot see you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Heavy traffic ahead.
Do not enter.
Railroad crossing.
Yield.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you not to enter the road or driveway ahead from your direction. If you see this sign, turn around and use a different route.

questions.question: When must you stop at an intersection?

options.text: When you see a flashing red light.
When you see a steady yellow light.
When you see a yellow arrow.
When you see a flashing yellow light.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see a flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same thing as a stop sign. You must stop completely, look both ways, and only go when the intersection is clear.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Reserved parking for persons with disabilities.
Slow-moving vehicle.
No U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reserved parking for persons with disabilities.
questions.explanation: This sign shows parking spaces reserved for people with disabilities. These spaces are for vehicles with disability license plates or disability parking permits only.

questions.question: When driving in fog, what should you use?

options.text: High beam headlights
Parking lights
Low beam headlights

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect back at you and make it harder to see.

questions.question: Which statement about right turns is true?

options.text: Swing wide to the left so you won't hit the curb.
You can turn right at a red light unless a sign says you cannot.
When turning right onto a four-lane road, end the turn in the far left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can turn right at a red light unless a sign says you cannot.
questions.explanation: After yielding to traffic and pedestrians, you may turn right at a red light unless a sign forbids it. Stay close to the right edge when turning right and turn into the lane nearest your current lane.

questions.question: Why is space between your vehicle and others important?

options.text: It stops distractions from other vehicles.
It gives you time to react to unexpected situations.
It keeps traffic moving at a safe speed.
It keeps other drivers alert.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you time to react to unexpected situations.
questions.explanation: Space between you and other vehicles gives you time to react if other drivers make mistakes.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: One mirror on each side eliminates blind spots.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
You can check blind spots by looking in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Large trucks have bigger blind spots than smaller vehicles, and you should avoid driving in them.

questions.question: You turn left from a two-way street onto a one-way street. Where should your car be?

options.text: In the right lane
In the center of the street
In the left lane
In the lane with the least traffic

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left lane
questions.explanation: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, finish the turn in the lane closest to the lane you just left.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle on a two-lane road with traffic going both ways, what should you do?

options.text: Return to your lane when you have enough space between you and the passed vehicle.
Stay in the left lane if you plan to turn left.
Return to the right side of the road right away.
Drive in either lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Return to your lane when you have enough space between you and the passed vehicle.
questions.explanation: After passing on a two-lane road, return to the right side when there is enough space between you and the vehicle you passed.

questions.question: At dawn, dusk, or in rain or snow, what should you do to let other drivers know you are there?

options.text: Turn up your dashboard lights.
Turn on your parking lights.
Turn on your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your headlights when you cannot see other vehicles clearly or when others cannot see you. Use your low beam headlights whenever you use your windshield wipers.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Turn on your high beam headlights.
Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Speed up to avoid an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, slow down and use your low beam lights. If fog is very thick and you cannot see, pull off the road and wait for it to clear.

questions.question: When can you legally drive around or under a railroad crossing gate?

options.text: Never
When you can see clearly in both directions
When the warning lights are not flashing

questions.correctAnswerText: Never
questions.explanation: Never drive around or under a lowered gate at a railroad crossing. After the gate is raised, wait until you can see clearly in both directions and confirm no trains are coming before crossing.

questions.question: What do speed limit signs show?

options.text: Possible speeds for the area
The highest or lowest speed you are legally allowed to drive
The speed to drive in heavy traffic
The speed to drive in poor conditions

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest or lowest speed you are legally allowed to drive
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs show the highest or lowest legal speed for that road. The maximum speed is for ideal conditions. You must slow down when conditions require it.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Slam on your brakes.
Hold the steering wheel tightly and slow down gradually.
Keep driving normally.
Turn on your emergency flashers and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel tightly and slow down gradually.
questions.explanation: Do not brake suddenly during a blowout. Grip the wheel firmly and stay in your lane. Let off the gas and slow down gradually. Once you are moving slowly, apply the brakes lightly and pull off the road to a safe spot.

questions.question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?

options.text: New drivers
Human error
Bad weather
Bad roads

questions.correctAnswerText: Human error
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers don't see other vehicles or when they do something unexpected. Communicate with other drivers to help prevent crashes.

questions.question: After passing another vehicle, when is it safe to move back to the right lane?

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you can no longer see the passed vehicle over your right shoulder.
When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Move back to your lane only when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. Always check your blind spots before moving back.

questions.question: Why should you signal continuously while turning?

options.text: It is illegal to turn off your signal before completing a turn.
It tells other drivers what you plan to do.
It is always unsafe to turn off a signal before completing a turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: It tells other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Signal when turning, changing lanes, slowing down, or stopping. This lets other drivers, motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians know your plans.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Lane ends.
No right turn.
Slippery when wet.
Two-way traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lane ends.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow and black. They tell you about road conditions and hazards ahead. This sign warns you that a lane is ending and traffic will need to merge safely.

questions.question: What does a double solid yellow line down the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is allowed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is not allowed.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Solid lines mean you cannot pass.

questions.question: What does this sign tell you?

options.text: No turns are allowed on the road.
The road narrows ahead.
There is a series of curves ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a series of curves ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They warn you about conditions coming up ahead. This sign warns you about a winding road.

questions.question: What do two solid yellow lines on the pavement mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is not allowed.
Passing is allowed at the top of a hill.
Passing is allowed during daylight only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mean traffic on the other side is moving in the opposite direction. Never cross two solid yellow lines to pass, no matter which direction you are going.

questions.question: Another driver is passing your car. What should you do?

options.text: Pull off the road.
Signal to the other driver when it is safe to pass.
Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed to help them pass safely.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed to help them pass safely.
questions.explanation: Stay right when another driver passes on the left. Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed so the passing vehicle can return to the right lane easily.

questions.question: If you get stranded in a snowstorm, what should you do?

options.text: Get out and go for help.
Lie down in your car and sleep.
Walk into the road to get other drivers' attention.
Stay in your car because you are most likely to be found there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car because you are most likely to be found there.
questions.explanation: Stay in your car if stranded in a snowstorm and wait for help. You are more likely to be found if you stay in your vehicle. Walking around in a snowstorm can be dangerous.
